title: Housekeeping
topic: A friend is putting a regular cleaner into the yearly budget
blurb: A friend just booked a cleaner and is doing the yearly math in the chat.
prompt: A friend just texted this in the group chat. If one line doesn't add up, tap it.

segments.label: The booking
segments.text: Finally booked a cleaner — $60 a visit, coming every two weeks.

segments.label: The month
segments.text: That's twice a month, so $120 a month.

segments.label: The year
segments.text: I'll just set aside $1,440 for the year and not think about it again.

segments.label: The offer
segments.text: If it works out, I'll send you their number.

conclusion: Every two weeks is twice a month, so $1,440 covers the year.

flaws.original: Every two weeks is 26 visits a year, not 24. At $60 that's $1,560, not $1,440.
flaws.corrupted: I'll just set aside $1,440 for the year and not think about it again.

diagnosis_choices.label: Every two weeks is 26 visits a year, not 24 — $1,440 is short $120.
Four months have five weeks, so those months get three visits and push the year to 28 visits ($1,680).
Every two weeks is 24 visits, and skipping Christmas and Thanksgiving drops the real bill to $1,320.
12 months times $120 is $1,540, not $1,440 — the multiplication itself is off by $100.

fix_choices.label: Add 4 extra visits for the 5-week months and set aside $1,680 for the year.
Re-multiply 12 × $120 as $1,540 so the yearly fund matches the monthly rate.
Drop two holiday visits from the schedule so the budget comes down to $1,320.

flaws.explanation: Every two weeks is 26 visits a year, not 24. That budget is short two cleanings.
flaws.why_tempting: 'Every two weeks' and 'twice a month' sound like the same sentence. The arithmetic from there is tidy — and already one step off.
flaws.catch_rule: 'Every two weeks' follows the calendar year, not the months: 52 ÷ 2 is 26, not 12 × 2.
flaws.hint: If they come every two weeks for a whole year, how many visits is that — 24, or something else?

practice.problem: A friend gets paid $2,000 every two weeks and says, 'That's $4,000 a month, $48,000 a year.' What's off?
practice.answer: Every two weeks is 26 paychecks a year, not 24. That's $52,000, not $48,000.

clean_segments: Finally booked a cleaner — $60 a visit, coming every two weeks.
That's twice a month, so $120 a month.
Every two weeks is 26 visits a year, not 24. At $60 that's $1,560, not $1,440.
If it works out, I'll send you their number.
clean_conclusion: Every two weeks is 26 visits a year, not 24. Budget $1,560, not $1,440.

diagnosis: $60 a visit doesn't include tips or cleaning supplies, so the per-visit base is understated.
'Every two weeks' means 14 days, which drifts across months and makes a fixed $60 rate impossible to budget.
A cleaner coming every two weeks comes 13 times a year (once every 4 weeks), not 26.
You can't budget a cleaner at $60 until you know if the first deep clean costs double.
fix: Add a 20% tip ($72 a visit) before multiplying out the year.
Ask the cleaner to bill a flat monthly fee instead of per visit.
Include a $120 first-visit deep-clean charge in the yearly budget.
Switch to a fixed 1st-and-15th calendar schedule instead of every two weeks.

diagnosis: Every two weeks is *more* than twice a month — two months a year have three visits ($180), not two.
Twice a month at $60 is $180 a month because months average 30 days (three 10-day gaps).
February only has 28 days, so every two weeks is only one visit in February ($60).
Saying '$120 a month' is right for 10 months, so the monthly average is $140, not $130.
fix: Average the year to $130 a month ($1,560 ÷ 12) instead of calling it $120 a month.
Budget $180 in the four 31-day months that pick up a third visit.
Lower February's budget to $60 to offset the longer months.
Book twice a month on fixed dates (1st and 15th) so it really stays $120 a month.

diagnosis: Sharing their number before you see the first clean risks recommending someone unreliable.
If your friend hires them on the alternate week, the cleaner's rate will jump past $60.
Recommending a cleaner priced at $1,440 a year misleads your friend by $120.
You shouldn't send their number until after the first 3-visit month proves they show up on schedule.
fix: Wait for two or three visits before passing along their contact info.
Warn your friend the yearly cost is $1,560, not $1,440, when you share the number.
Ask the cleaner if they offer a referral discount before sending their number.
Check if they have open biweekly slots before offering the contact.
